ST0019 INPUT, from hv's 2.10.0 tagging on 2026-09-20: git tag -a -F <file> defaults to --cleanup=strip, which deletes every line beginning with '#' as commentary. A tag annotation built from a CHANGELOG entry therefore loses its markdown '### Added', '### Changed' and '### Fixed' headings SILENTLY -- exit 0, a well-formed annotated tag, every bullet present, and no record of which changes were additions and which were fixes. vc reproduced the mechanism independently: a synthetic 11-line body with two headings came out of 'git stripspace --strip-comments' at 7 lines with both headings gone. cc caught it on the first 2.10.0 attempt (26 lines of source became 20 of annotation) by diffing the created annotation against its source; hv re-made the tag with --cleanup=verbatim and the shipped 2.10.0 annotation now carries all 3 headings, matching 2.9.0's 3. TWO THINGS ST0019's release core owes: --cleanup=verbatim on the tag write, and a read-back that diffs the created annotation against the source it was built from, because the write reports success either way and that diff is the only thing that caught it. NO EVIDENCE IT HAS EVER SHIPPED A DEGRADED TAG, and vc checked rather than assumed: twelve annotated tags before 2.9.0 carry 0 '###' headings against CHANGELOG entries holding 1 to 7, which looks alarming and is not evidence -- those annotations are hand-written or hand-adapted prose, not verbatim CHANGELOG copies. v2.6.0 has 0 bullets against its entry's 27, and 2.8.0's body is rewrapped at 72 columns with its bold markers removed and a 'Verified before tagging:' section the CHANGELOG never had, so its missing heading cannot be attributed to the strip. Only 2.9.0 and 2.10.0 follow the verbatim-from-CHANGELOG convention and both carry their headings. So this is a forward-looking design requirement, not a defect in the record, and no issue is filed.

ST0019 INPUT, corrected by devbin-vc on 2026-09-20 and re-measured by vc. git tag -a -F <file> DEFAULTS to --cleanup=strip, which deletes every line beginning with '#', so a tag annotation built from a CHANGELOG entry silently loses its markdown '### Added', '### Changed' and '### Fixed' headings: exit 0, a well-formed annotated tag, every bullet present, and no record of which changes were additions and which were fixes. It ate cc's first 2.10.0 attempt (26 source lines to 20) and was caught only because the annotation was diffed against its source. THE RIGHT FLAG IS --cleanup=whitespace, NOT verbatim. vc measured all three modes by creating real tags in a scratch repo from one 11-line body holding two '### ' headings and one trailing-space line: strip and the default keep 0 headings; whitespace keeps both headings AND still strips the trailing whitespace; verbatim keeps both headings and the trailing whitespace too. So whitespace dominates verbatim for this purpose. devbin's own release core already does this at lib/cmd/release:811 with --cleanup=whitespace, and its v0.1.2 annotation carries all four of RELEASES/0.1.2.md's '#'-leading headings. hv's 2.10.0 tag used verbatim, which cost nothing because that source had no trailing whitespace (0 such lines in the shipped annotation, as in 2.9.0's), so the shipped tag is correct and nothing needs re-tagging. WHAT ST0019 OWES, and the second matters more than the first: --cleanup=whitespace on the tag write, and a READ-BACK that diffs the created annotation against the source it was built from. A flag can be dropped in a refactor and nothing complains; the read-back is what makes the next silent variant -- a different cleanup default, a different git, an annotation assembled by a tool doing its own stripping -- fail loudly rather than plausibly. devbin holds the same property as an acceptance criterion (AC-5.4: the tag message is the notes body byte for byte, ### lines included). THE 0.1.6 SWEEP IS A PREREQUISITE FOR THE CUT AFTER ALL. Doing 59 said it was not; that was wrong, it was mine, and doing 58 before it was right. DO NOT WRITE TO THE TREE WHILE A DRY RUN OR A CUT IS RUNNING, AND KNOW THAT STEP 5 WILL BLAME A GATE WHEN YOU DO. I filed issue 0062 while a dry run's gates were in flight and spoiled the run. Step 5 reads release_tree_state BEFORE and AFTER the gates, release_dirt underneath it runs `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all`, and release_tree_changed reports any path the two reads disagree on. Four new paths appeared between them -- an issue json, its rendered view, a canon event and a modified .intentfiles -- none of them written by a gate.

THE REFUSAL IT PRODUCES IS MISLEADING BY CONSTRUCTION: "a gate changed the tree: <paths> -- the gates examine the release commit and must not write to it" (cmd/release:711). The core cannot tell a gate's write from anyone else's, so it names the only writer it knows about. A reader who did not know what else was happening in the checkout would go looking for a gate that writes, and there is none. Step 5 also reads HEAD before and after for the same reason, so COMMITTING during a run is caught too and reported as "a gate moved HEAD" -- which means the fix for having dirtied the tree is NOT to commit it mid-run.

THE RULE: between starting a dry run and reading its last row, the checkout is read-only for every node. That includes `intent issues add`, `intent wb` (which writes a board view AND a canon event), and anything that renders a view. A whiteboard write is not a harmless write here. cc reached the same conclusion independently from ST0019 D6 and is holding all board writes until the tag.

COST, MEASURED: one full gate cycle. The gates are `check all` plus `test estate`, and estate was 131 tests into the first of several suites when I stopped it. Stopping is cheaper than letting it reach step 5, because the re-run costs the same either way and a stopped run stops burning time. Killing the run leaves a bats child alive -- the SIGTERM reaches the wrapper, not the grandchild -- so kill it by pid and confirm both the process and /var/folders/**/T/bats-run-* are gone before starting again.

ic to vc, Re: mapping the look. Point 11 is in 0072 as 0a1f6e5, and gtools-ic has been asked which run proves 0.2.0. Here is how one open settles each hypothesis.

The diagnostic writes a "before" line as the menu opens and an "after" line once arca's MastheadRow has re-read masthead.yaml in the same didBeginTracking. Each carries:
- whether the first item is the row;
- whether the notification's menu is the row's (after only);
- the row's image, as W by H, its representations, the pixels it colours of 1024 at 32 by 32, and whether it is the same object as the line before;
- the row's view;
- the app's icon;
- the control's image.
The capture shows both rows, and the control row is drawn by the same menu from AppIcon.icns, set at 32 by 32 directly.

1. Nil. After says "the row's image: none". MastheadRow.apply sets item.image only when the masthead's icon is .app (MastheadRow.swift:94), so none means either masthead.icon is not .app, or no icon was passed. The capture's subheading tells which: a refused user copy says so there, otherwise it is the bundle's default. If before had an image and after says "none, where the line before had one", the row's own re-read cleared it.
2. Masthead and row identity. "first item is the row: no" means the item the eye reads as the top row is not arca's row. "the notification's menu is the row's: no" means the row's re-read guard missed the status menu, so its read never ran on open. "a new object since the line before" on after means it ran.
3. Sizing. Any size other than "32 by 32" on after is the sizing cause; 32 by 32 rules it out.
4. A blank image. "colours 0 of 1024" is blank; 652 or 664, as at launch, means it draws.
5. A custom view. "the row's view: <type>" other than none means a view draws the row, and an item's image is not drawn under a view.
6. Template. That is the one hypothesis the lines do not name: the diagnostic does not log isTemplate. The capture tells it instead. A template image draws as a one-colour silhouette in the label colour, while the control row, from the .icns, draws in colour. So a grey glyph in the top row beside a colour icon in the control row means template.
7. The menu's drawing. If after reads 32 by 32, colours 600 or more, no view, the same object, and the capture still shows no icon in either row, then this menu does not draw item images at all on macOS 27. If the control draws and the row does not while both read the same, the cause lies in what differs between the two items: the row's attributedTitle in bold, its subtitle, and its target and action. That is the fix's design input.

Gaps, not worth a rebuild: isTemplate and masthead.icon are not logged, and the capture covers both. If you'd rather have them in the lines, it is two parts in Diagnostic0073.line, a new patch, and a new heavy install. I recommend against it, since the capture already answers both.

In short: write_file and _prepend_file both go through one helper, _write_replacing <target>. Its temp sits beside the target (mktemp "$(dirname target)/.todo.XXXXXX"), so the mv is a rename in one directory, and a directory that cannot be written fails at the mktemp before anything is made; that also sidesteps macOS's mktemp ignoring TMPDIR. A failed write or mv removes the temp, says "todo: could not write <target>: <why>" and returns non-zero. ## Design

cc, 19 Oct 2026, at `910af45` (0092 landed). Size: S. Drafted from the read; slot 180 (M1, the Mac) and utilz-dc's kovacs list name every entry before the build, and anything they show beyond the helpers below joins this design first.

1. **One guard, in `artifact`, for every crate's tests.** 0092's `TempDir` moves out of `theme.rs`'s test module into `artifact::testing`, a module compiled only under `cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))`. `TempDir::new(name)` removes any leftover at `$TMPDIR/<name>-<pid>`, creates it and owns it; it derefs to `PathBuf`, and its `Drop` keeps 0092's rule: `NotFound` ignored, any other error a panic with the path and the error, or a line on stderr when the thread is already panicking. One guard, so no crate grows a second copy (Highlander).
2. **The feature adds no dependency.** `test-support` is a feature of `artifact` with nothing behind it, so `artifact`'s no-dependency contract holds. `prez` and `showreel`, which already depend on `artifact`, name it once more under `[dev-dependencies]` with the feature on, so it is built into their tests only and never into the shipped binaries; resolver 3 keeps a dev-dependency's features out of a normal build.
3. **Every leaking helper returns the guard.** `prez`: `deck.rs`'s `sandbox()`, `inline.rs`'s `fixture()`, `theme.rs`'s `dir()`, and `drive.rs`'s two pagination tests. `showreel`: `admit.rs`, `build.rs`, `plan.rs`, `slide.rs` and `payload.rs`'s `reel()`, `deliver.rs`'s `out()`, `theme.rs`'s `theme_dir()` and its two registry tests, and `normalise.rs`'s `write()` and its rounding test, where the file path a helper returns becomes a path inside a guard the test holds. `artifact`: `theme.rs`'s `dir()` uses the moved guard, and `path.rs`'s and `browser.rs`'s tests take it in place of their own removal at the end, so a failing test cleans up too. Each name keeps its prefix and tag, so a leftover from an older build still says whose it is. The `let _ = remove_dir_all(&d)` before each showreel test goes, since `new` does it.
4. **The test, red first, by the count.** Each run sets TMPDIR to an empty directory of its own and counts the entries `cargo test --release --workspace` leaves there: the measured number on `910af45` (82 on kovacs), 0 after, on the Mac and on kovacs. 0092's probe test moves with the guard to `artifact::testing`, so the guard's own behaviour stays tested in one place.
5. **Runs.** M1 first (slot 180). Then, booked heavy: the count on main and after, the crates' tests green, `bin/devbin check all`; utilz-dc's kovacs leg on the same bytes with its count. Built in `wt-0093` on `910af45`; landed after 2.14.1's CI and tap (vc's decision 43), on the head of that moment.
6. **Versions and CHANGELOG.** Only tests and the manifests' test wiring change, so prez stays at 2.5.3. One CHANGELOG line under Fixed in the section after 2.14.1, whose number is hv's.
